title.narrative: Output 6.1.2 Comprehensive list of all public corporations in FBiH and BIH institutions level published (BiH).

description.narrative: Output 6.1.2 Comprehensive list of all public corporations in FBiH and BIH institutions level published (BiH).

comment.narrative: Center for Civil Initiatives an NGO published a comprehensive list of public corporations in BiH that provides basic information on public corporations though financial information is not available. This complements the list of public corporations that was introduced at the FIA for FBiH but that is not comprehensive. A registry for the RS is not regularly updated. CD support to FBiH began the consolidation of a database of financial information of SOEs and the drafting of an SOE and ownership policy though delays in the creation of an oversight unit has stalled work. BD captured financial information on SOEs for the period 2019 2021 in the SOE Health Check tool.

comment.narrative: An Excelbased model was developed to estimate POEs financial performance indicators to be included in the fiscal risk statement. An initial assessment and quantification of fiscal risks from POEs was prepared by the Ministry of Finance and is included in the 20222024 MTEF and 2023 ERP.

title.narrative: Output 6.1.2 Comprehensive list of all public corporations in FBiH and BIH institutions level published (BiH).

description.narrative: Output 6.1.2 Comprehensive list of all public corporations in FBiH and BIH institutions level published (BiH).

comment.narrative: Center for Civil Initiatives an NGO published a comprehensive list of public corporations in BiH that provides basic information on public corporations though financial information is not available. This complements the list of public corporations that was introduced at the FIA for FBiH but that is not comprehensive. A registry for the RS is not regularly updated. CD support to FBiH began the consolidation of a database of financial information of SOEs and the drafting of an SOE and ownership policy though delays in the creation of an oversight unit has stalled work. BD captured financial information on SOEs for the period 2019 2021 in the SOE Health Check tool.

AL Disclosure and management of contingent liabilities and other specific risks are more comprehensive but there is still room to strengthen the analysis of these risks and scope of the fiscal risk statement. BiH Actions on disclosure and management of contingent liabilities and other specific risks included in PFM strategies. Outline for annual SOE report was developed in FBiH. KOS The fiscal risk chapter in the MTEF discusses systematic macroeconomic risks and specific risks i Risk of contingent liabilities arising from onborrowed loans and credit guarantees ii Underexecution of capital expenditures iii Pressure to increase transfer spending iv Fiscal risks from revenue collection v Outstanding liabilities vi Fiscal risks from court cases. The MTEF and 2023 ERP also includes quantifications of fiscal risks from POEs. MNE While substantial training has been delivered on assessing the risks and costs of PPP contracts to a number of Ministry of Finance and line Ministry stakeholders there are no disclosures on PPP risk so far.MKD Jointly with the Development Bank of North Macedonia a model has been developed to support the assessment of the credit risks of the guarantee portfolio introduced to mitigate the impact of the COVID19 pandemic. The Ministry of Finance however does not use the tool and awaits the OBL before systemically addressing nondebt related contingent liabilities. SRB Analysis of risks related to the credit guarantee scheme introduced to mitigate the impact of COVID19 on the economy has improved through the development of an analytical model.

comment.narrative: AL Comprehensiveness and timeliness of monitoring and reporting publicBIH Outline for an annual SOE report in FBiH developed. RS considers developing central oversight function through WB support based on FAD HQ mission findings and recommendations. The plan for developing or updating the lists of public corporations was stated within the 4 PFM reform strategies. This will be the basis for BiH comprehensive list. KOSAn annual POE Performance Report is prepared by MoE but pending for adoption in the Parliament for FY 2019. MoF is responsible for analyzing POErelated fiscal risks and now includes POE fiscal risk analysis in the MTEFs the analysis mostly focusses on major POEs.MKD Financial data revenue expenditure and lossprofit before tax information for 29 SOEs is published in the Fiscal Strategy but analyses on SOEs do not exist.SRB Apr 21 Fiscal Risk Unit is established and operational. Fiscal risks are discussed within the Fiscal Strategies.

description.narrative: Outputs 1.1.2 (North Macedonia)Improved Compliance Risk Management (CRM) plan 2022 developed by 2021.

comment.narrative: As a result of a technical assistance assignment in November 2021 the PRO staff across five sectors have agreed to collaborate in a trial of risk management processes. The collaboration will involve the creation and implementation of a compliance plan CP for businesses providing personal services. While a positive step this does not constitute a proper CP across all major identified compliance risks. As of June 2022 there was no progress with developing such a plan beyond a mere proposal from the head of the RMU. A draft compliance plan 2022 exists however as of July 2022 it has not been adopted.

comment.narrative: 6 countries AL North MK ME SER XK BA

AL A CIS is in place. A CMC exists and a modern CRM methodology is being implemented. BA The CRM unit is in place. ITA is gradually phasing in modern CRM methodology.KOS TAK is gradually phasing in modern CRM methodology. A risk management department is in place. MNE First generation annual compliance plan has been developed. MKD By way of regress the RMU is no longer staffed only the head of unit is in place. CRM is not driving operational decisions. Disjoint analysis teams specialist exists in various units. For instance the General Tax Inspectorate has 45 specialists whose task is the analysis of legal and natural persons tax risks with varying workload between 50100 of their working time. During HQ Mission Spring 2022 and LTX visit Summer 2022 the management made a commitment to staff the RMU the second half of 2022. SRB With considerable CD assistance in 202122 the STA has improved its handling of risks and risk data. IMFassisted VAT gap assessment based on RAGAP is upcoming in 2022. Efiscalization finalized on May 1 2022.

comment.narrative: As a result of a technical assistance assignment in November 2021 the PRO staff across five sectors have agreed to collaborate in a trial of risk management processes. The collaboration will involve the creation and implementation of a compliance plan CP for businesses providing personal services. While a positive step this does not constitute a proper CP across all major identified compliance risks. As of June 2022 there was no progress with developing such a plan beyond a mere proposal from the head of the RMU. A draft compliance plan 2022 exists however as of July 2022 it has not been adopted.

MNE First generation annual compliance plan has been developed. MKD By way of regress the RMU is no longer staffed only the head of unit is in place. CRM is not driving operational decisions. Disjoint analysis teams specialist exists in various units. For instance the General Tax Inspectorate has 45 specialists whose task is the analysis of legal and natural persons tax risks with varying workload between 50100 of their working time. During HQ Mission Spring 2022 and LTX visit Summer 2022 the management made a commitment to staff the RMU the second half of 2022. description.narrative: Output 1.2.0 (Aggregated)Strategic andOperational Plansadopted and implemented

comment.narrative: AL 1. Strategic and operational plans are in place and monitored regularly by the executives. A draft strategic plan 20222026 is prepared but not yet approved as the approval is predicated on the completion of the MTRS. KOS A comprehensive new Strategic Plan for 202226 is established with help from this project. It sets out a 5year reform agenda to deliver sustainable improvements in revenue collection and support the development of tax administration reform efforts. MNE Rudimentary bottom up operational plans developed however they are not riskpriority based or aligned to resource availability.MKDSystem of strategic and operational planning is in place. However it seems to be too formalistic and does not meet the needs of the executive and management. Strategic planning is done as a summary of bottomup initiatives which need better coordination and harmonization within the PRO. The PRO however monitors its strengths and weaknesses adequately.SRB Strategic and operational plans are available and used. The STA must pay more attention to detailed implementation planning assigning concrete responsibilities and resources.

The strategic plan is rather a summary of units initiatives and needs better harmonization across the PRO while setting compliance improvements as the primary goal of the whole organization. Some initiatives are evidently underresourced. The strategic plan is however adequate and candid in relation to the PROs strengths and weaknesses.

comment.narrative: AL 1. Strategic and operational plans are in place and monitored regularly by the executives. A draft strategic plan 20222026 is prepared but not yet approved as the approval is predicated on the completion of the MTRS. KOS A comprehensive new Strategic Plan for 202226 is established with help from this project. It sets out a 5year reform agenda to deliver sustainable improvements in revenue collection and support the development of tax administration reform efforts. MNE Rudimentary bottom up operational plans developed however they are not riskpriority based or aligned to resource availability.MKDSystem of strategic and operational planning is in place. However it seems to be too formalistic and does not meet the needs of the executive and management. Strategic planning is done as a summary of bottomup initiatives which need better coordination and harmonization within the PRO. The PRO however monitors its strengths and weaknesses adequately.SRB Strategic and operational plans are available and used. The STA must pay more attention to detailed implementation planning assigning concrete responsibilities and resources.

description.narrative: Output 1.3.0 (Aggregated)Appropriate institutional settings in place

comment.narrative: 5 countries AL North MK ME SER XK

AL GDT has a management committee structure in place. Several working groups support the work of the management committees i.e. the fiscalization project AEOI with other jurisdictions central register of bank accounts consolidation of arrears collection. KOSInitial actions have been taken to modernize the regional offices network through the consolidation of tax debt collection into one office for all of Kosovo. Work on designing options for further rationalization of the regional structure is planned to commence with the help of this project. Implementing major design changes before the scheduled end of this project may be challenging as the mobilization of political support and the implementation itself will take time.MNEDue to challenges that affected the RA reform agenda it is necessary with a new HQ assessment to establish whether improvements are still in place and any new improvements are built up. The challenges are merging revenue and customs administrations changes in organizational structure frequent changes in management in the last two years other reform projects and the administrative capacity to handle changes in the approach to tax compliance and daily operational work. The October 2022 HQ mission will verify.MKD. Over time the PRO has introduced changes in its structure however further key reforms are still necessary. The current structure is not optimal for wellcoordinated reform management processes and permanent structures are missing or not staffed for planning and coordinating effective compliance risk management. SRB Key executive committees are now in place and operational. Functional sectors must provide more dedicated resources to reform process and project organization setup must be strengthened.

title.narrative: Output 1.3.1 (Albania)Optimal Regional Office structure in place by July 2021.

description.narrative: Output 1.3.1 (Albania)Optimal Regional Office structure in place by July 2021.

comment.narrative: Work on establishing an optimal regional office structure is well underway. The current development points in the direction of eventually arriving at a structure consisting of 3 regional offices SouthMid North organized in a number of large specialist departments e.g. debt tax audit taxpayer services. In addition there may be a number of very small field offices in remote areas to provide services to taxpayers see above. This structure will not be implemented by end2022 as it would take time to mobilize political support for it and implementation would require time too.

title.narrative: Output 1.3.2 (North Macedonia)New HQ and field office structure adopted by 2020

description.narrative: Output 1.3.2 (North Macedonia)New HQ and field office structure adopted by 2020

comment.narrative: Meeting Target Completion proved to be challenging as all discussions on structural reform were put on hold due to the pandemic and two elections general in 2020 and municipal in late 2021. However certain structural changes were introduced due to abolition of nontax functions e.g. forensic accounting and due to technological progress no need for large numbers of data input and return management officials. A review of the PRO structure originally planned for 2020 was put on hold due to the pandemic. Such reviews are required every four years or if there are significant changes in the organization. The PRO is planning to introduce some structural changes in 2022 based on own analyses and on recommendations from various missions and CD assignments.

All the remaining operation functions e.g. taxpayer services tax audit are allocated to 10 regional offices. The balance between these offices in terms of their resources and their workload is not adequate. A new business model is required.

comment.narrative: AL1. Information on the main areas of core tax obligations and entitlements is readily available through various channels and the GDT provides a broad range of proactive taxpayer education programs. Information is not tailored to meet the needs of tax intermediaries and disadvantaged groups. 2. The GDT consults on an ad hoc basis with key taxpayer groups and intermediaries to identify administrative processes and product deficiencies and stakeholders are involved in the design or testing of taxpayer service programs only on an ad hoc basis. Taxpayers are not always alerted to changes in the law or administrative policy before the law or policy takes effect. The use of prefilled tax declarations for taxable businesses is increasing. The design and the content of tax declarations and other forms are reviewed periodically.

Taxpayers are not always alerted to changes in the law or administrative policy before the law or policy takes effect. The use of prefilled tax declarations for taxable businesses is increasing. The design and the content of tax declarations and other forms are reviewed periodically.

comment.narrative: A properly organized LTO is in place that manages all taxpayers that meet the threshold. Based on guidance provided by an IMF expert the LTO is going through the lengthy process of risk profiling every single taxpayer using the international recognized risk differentiation framework. A total of 500 600 taxpayers have now been profiled. Tax audit remains the weakest component of the LTO. Attracting highly competent auditors to work with large segment taxpayers is very challenging given the current remuneration levels.

comment.narrative: The March 2019 HQ mission provided recommendations to improve tax audit function. FAD advice in respect of audit has not yet gained full traction and implementation of the earlier recommendations. Training activities performed in 2021 and 2022 with Slovakia as a Twinning partner on transfer pricing and international taxation.By October 2021 there have been some improvements in audits of the cash economy. Also audit results have somewhat improved in 2021 vs 2020 hit rate 39.9 vs. 36.6 and yield MKD198 Bn vs. MKD1.18 Bn.An assignment on LTO in April 2022 provided advice on ensuring effectiveness of audit activities. LTO bound to implement progressively. Suggestion to move target to Dec22.

title.narrative: Output 2.4.1 (Albania)Large Taxpayer Office (LTO) is an efficiently organized department with all taxpayers who meet the LTO threshold under closemanagement by 2021

description.narrative: Output 2.4.1 (Albania)Large Taxpayer Office (LTO) is an efficiently organized department with all taxpayers who meet the LTO threshold under closemanagement by 2021

comment.narrative: A properly organized LTO is in place that manages all taxpayers that meet the threshold. Based on guidance provided by an IMF expert the LTO is going through the lengthy process of risk profiling every single taxpayer using the international recognized risk differentiation framework. A total of 500 600 taxpayers have now been profiled. Tax audit remains the weakest component of the LTO. Attracting highly competent auditors to work with large segment taxpayers is very challenging given the current remuneration levels.

title.narrative: Output 2.4.2 (North Macedonia)Improved audit processes developed and in place.

description.narrative: Output 2.4.2 (North Macedonia)Improved audit processes developed and in place.

comment.narrative: The March 2019 HQ mission provided recommendations to improve tax audit function. FAD advice in respect of audit has not yet gained full traction and implementation of the earlier recommendations. Training activities performed in 2021 and 2022 with Slovakia as a Twinning partner on transfer pricing and international taxation.By October 2021 there have been some improvements in audits of the cash economy. Also audit results have somewhat improved in 2021 vs 2020 hit rate 39.9 vs. 36.6 and yield MKD198 Bn vs. MKD1.18 Bn.An assignment on LTO in April 2022 provided advice on ensuring effectiveness of audit activities. LTO bound to implement progressively. Suggestion to move target to Dec22.

title.narrative: Output 2.2.0 (Aggregated)Management of taxarrears improved

description.narrative: Output 2.2.0 (Aggregated)Management of taxarrears improved

comment.narrative: 4 countries AL North MK SER XK

AL Despite the successful consolidation of the arrears collection function to three collection centers plus the LTO the consolidation initiative has not yet had sufficient impact on the debt situation the trends are still upward. BiH Review of the current practice shows a need for its improvement and expansion to the additional thirdparty data sources which have been identified. Implementation plan developed pending approval from the management of all administration. Proposed changes of MOU.KOSThe persistent growth in tax arrears appears to have been arrested but debt levels remain excessive. A clear plan is now in place to reduce the level of total core tax arrears to no more than 10 percent of total core tax revenue. At the center of the plan is the consolidation of collection enforcement staff into a single centralized collection center which will use more targeted and streamlined debt recovery practices. Plans to writeoff old and uncollectible debts are running behind schedule. MNE Due to challenges affecting the RA reform agenda it a new HQ assessment is necessary to establish whether improvements are still in place and any new improvements are built up. The challenges are merging revenue and customs administrations changes in organizational structure frequent changes in management in the last two years other reform projects and the administrative capacity to handle changes in the approach to tax compliance and daily operational work. The Oct 2022 HQ mission will verify. 1. 2 and 3 Needs to be reassessed. MKD The reform of arrears management process started in 2019. Some improvements took place in 2020. However stocks of debt remain large and fluctuate from year to year. While the COVID19 pandemic has not led to significant increase in debts further improvement has proved difficult. The VAT debt to revenue has improved in 2021 however the share of old debt over 12 months has also increased.SRB Large stock of uncollectable debt remains an issue legal solutions needed. Actions are underway to identifyquantify and separate from the collectable debt pool but due to sheer volumes of old debt critical decisions must be made. CD assistance provided in FY21. As a result more writeoffs of obsolete debt are taking place. The issue of competence for mass writeoffs must be elevated to the political level.

title.narrative: Output 2.2.1 (Albania)Best practice automated riskbased procedures in place for all VAT refunds.

description.narrative: Output 2.2.1 (Albania)Best practice automated riskbased procedures in place for all VAT refunds.

comment.narrative: Improved riskbased refund screening and workflows have significantly reduced the average interval between refund requests and reimbursements. Further recent improvements include online refund applications and fasttracked refunds for predominant exporters. The stock of arrears has recently been fully cleared and legitimate refund claims are now fully paid within the statutory time limit. Interest payments are made on delayed refund payments upon the taxpayers request. The GDT plans to change the IT system to pay interest automatically.

title.narrative: Output 2.2.2 (North Macedonia)New procedures (including debt case management system) for improvedarrears collection outcomes introduced.

description.narrative: Output 2.2.2 (North Macedonia)New procedures (including debt case management system) for improvedarrears collection outcomes introduced.

comment.narrative: The reform of arrears management process started in 2019 but debt case management system is not yet in place. As a prerequisite the PRO has intensified efforts to introduce an IT upgrade to the tax accounting software with the help of the MoF an action plan was adopted in July 2021.In May 2021 the PRO adopted a phased approach to newly incurred debt and it is now obligatory for the operational level staff to start recovery procedures with soft measures.In August 2021 changes were introduced to guidelines on tax debt deferral to facilitate less burdensome amendment process of valid installment schedules in case of new debt.Improvements are being sought through the implementation of a Center of Excellence within the tax arrears function following a respective TA assignment by the IMF.New software is planned and ordered from the IT sector for mass processes warnings forced collection of funds in the bank writeoff due to obsolescence. This should be automated through the tax accounting software module from Jan 1 2024.

Interest payments are made on delayed refund payments upon the taxpayers request. The GDT plans to change the IT system to pay interest automatically.

title.narrative: Output 2.2.0 (Aggregated)Management of taxarrears improved

description.narrative: Output 2.2.0 (Aggregated)Management of taxarrears improved

comment.narrative: 4 countries AL North MK SER XK

AL Despite the successful consolidation of the arrears collection function to three collection centers plus the LTO the consolidation initiative has not yet had sufficient impact on the debt situation the trends are still upward. BiH Review of the current practice shows a need for its improvement and expansion to the additional thirdparty data sources which have been identified. Implementation plan developed pending approval from the management of all administration. Proposed changes of MOU.KOSThe persistent growth in tax arrears appears to have been arrested but debt levels remain excessive. A clear plan is now in place to reduce the level of total core tax arrears to no more than 10 percent of total core tax revenue. At the center of the plan is the consolidation of collection enforcement staff into a single centralized collection center which will use more targeted and streamlined debt recovery practices. Plans to writeoff old and uncollectible debts are running behind schedule. MNE Due to challenges affecting the RA reform agenda it a new HQ assessment is necessary to establish whether improvements are still in place and any new improvements are built up. The challenges are merging revenue and customs administrations changes in organizational structure frequent changes in management in the last two years other reform projects and the administrative capacity to handle changes in the approach to tax compliance and daily operational work. The Oct 2022 HQ mission will verify. 1. 2 and 3 Needs to be reassessed. MKD The reform of arrears management process started in 2019. Some improvements took place in 2020. However stocks of debt remain large and fluctuate from year to year. While the COVID19 pandemic has not led to significant increase in debts further improvement has proved difficult. The VAT debt to revenue has improved in 2021 however the share of old debt over 12 months has also increased.SRB Large stock of uncollectable debt remains an issue legal solutions needed. Actions are underway to identifyquantify and separate from the collectable debt pool but due to sheer volumes of old debt critical decisions must be made. CD assistance provided in FY21. As a result more writeoffs of obsolete debt are taking place. The issue of competence for mass writeoffs must be elevated to the political level.
